chapter: Memphis, Oklahoma, the Kirk band and Kansas City
title: Sorting out the chronology: Chicago, the Pearl and joining the band
summary: She and the interviewer untangle the order: Chicago recording was the band's start, the Pearl came before, and the Pearl is where she became a regular member.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Yes... When we went to Chicago to record for Jack Kapp, that was the beginning of the success of the band and then later on Jack Kapp moved to New York and became Decca. I guess that was less than a year and Joe Glaser came out of Chicago. Then when they had those hits, that was in '33 or '34.
So it was, in other words, more or less from the time of the Brunswick recordings in Chicago that this was the time the band began to rise?
Then after that you did the Pearl and then after that you did the Savoy, is that right?
We did the Pearl - now I'm confused. We did the Pearl Theatre before I was called to Chicago to record for Brunswick.
...It was after that that you played at the Savoy...
I played the Savoy again, but the next time they played I was with the band.
Was it the first time at the Savoy that you actually became a regular member of the band?
No, the first time I became a regular member was in the Pearl Theatre when they had the double piano. See they used me on the show with them.
And then they kept - Jack was dropped after that?
They were dropped after that afternoon and then it was maybe a month before we went to Kansas City.
I'm sure it is. 'Cause if you get those dates wrong.
Kansas City became more or less home territory for you, right?
